candidate.blueprint_locator: Physiological Integrity — Basic Care and Comfort: provide comfort measures, hygiene, and assistance with activities that support the client's physical comfort and recovery.
candidate.blueprint_topic: Basic Care and Comfort — postpartum perineal hygiene and comfort
candidate.educational_objective: Teach postpartum perineal care using gentle warm-water cleansing, patting dry, frequent sanitary-pad changes, and hand hygiene while avoiding unnecessary fragranced or antiseptic additives unless specifically directed.

options.A: I can use warm water from a peri-bottle after voiding or bowel movements, pat the area dry, change sanitary pads frequently, and wash my hands before and after pad changes.
options.B: I should avoid cleansing the perineum between showers because repeated contact with water delays healing.
options.C: I should add antiseptic or fragranced products to the peri-bottle routinely so the wound remains sterile.
options.D: I can leave the same sanitary pad in place unless it becomes completely saturated because frequent pad changes irritate the wound.

candidate.rationale: A is correct. Current NCBI postpartum nursing guidance describes using a peri-bottle filled with warm water to gently cleanse and soothe the perineal and rectal area after voiding and bowel movements, followed by gentle drying. Current postnatal-care guidance also emphasizes good perineal hygiene, including regular cleansing, frequent sanitary-pad changes, and hand hygiene before and after pad changes. B is incorrect because gentle cleansing is part of routine postpartum care. C is incorrect because additives or medicated products should not be placed in cleansing water unless specifically directed; routine fragranced or antiseptic products are unnecessary. D is incorrect because frequent sanitary-pad changes are part of recommended perineal hygiene and allow ongoing observation of lochia and wound condition.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Postpartum perineal self-care includes gentle warm-water cleansing with a peri-bottle, gentle drying, frequent sanitary-pad changes, and hand hygiene; routine additives are not required unless directed.
